baer-heitev/2:_: Before. In Matz he wrote they kindle before and he will give you. Magen Avraham wrote: one who forgot Atah Chonantanu should make havdalah and then kindle, for now people practice not to kindle before havdalah in prayer — if so forbidden to kindle since he did not make havdalah; nevertheless in congregation do not do so — only the one who makes havdalah kindles and afterward makes havdalah — end. Tosefet Yom Tov wrote the Gaon Maharal of Prague instituted havdalah first lest he forget havdalah in prayer and commit prohibition in kindling; he concludes so one should practice; so Taz l'maaseh — havdalah in his home at least first then Hanukkah light — end. {Rama: In Eliyah Rabbah he brought to halacha that always kindle first then make havdalah and rejected Taz's words with two hands — end}:
biur-halacha/2:_: They kindle, etc., before havdalah — see Mishna Berurah in what we wrote in the name of Taz; truly many Acharonim uphold his method — havdalah precedes — Maharal of Prague, Tosefet Yom Tov [brought in Eliyah Rabbah], Peri Chadash, Dagul MeRevavah, and many Acharonim uphold Shulchan Aruch and Rama — namely Magen Avraham, Eliyah Rabbah, Gra, Beit Meir; in Chemdat Moshe he answered all Taz's proofs; in She'elat Yaavetz he agrees with Shulchan Aruch; indeed this dispute is heard among the living and already divided among the early ones, aside from what Beit Yosef brought that Terumat HaDeshen holds Hanukkah light precedes and Maharil, Agur, and Kol Bo hold likewise; R' Avudraham wrote some make havdalah first — in Meiri our custom is to kindle Hanukkah light before havdalah; in Eshkol laws of Hanukkah: I saw many bless before havdalah — to the writer it seems error, etc. — see there [see Machatzit HaShekel, Birkat Yosef, Zechor L'Avraham]. Therefore correct to practice as several Acharonim agreed: in synagogue do not change custom always practiced to kindle Hanukkah light first; at home — whoever follows his custom; also Peri Megadim wrote do not rebuke anyone for he has whom to rely on.
chatam-sofer/1:_: Taz s.k. 1 in d.h. all this, etc., Shabbat unlike, etc. NB: requires study in Ra'avad Mishnah 6 chapter 8 of Berachot: blessings we can do without appearing as burden, such as candle and spices — we precede to Birkat HaMazon — end; meaning: but havdalah we delay lest it appear as burden. Here we see blessing on candle without havdalah wording is not release of Shabbat — unlike Taz.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (ב) [Seif 2] They kindle Hanukkah light in synagogue before havdalah — so Beit Yosef in the name of Terumat HaDeshen siman 60 that they kindle Hanukkah light in synagogue before havdalah to delay taking out the day; Radbaz wrote some kindle it after making havdalah on the cup and then recite Yiftach (the prayer opening after havdalah on the cup), etc. — end Beit Yosef. He ruled here in Shulchan Aruch like Terumat HaDeshen; so Darkei Moshe — Maharil, Agur, Kol Bo wrote like Terumat HaDeshen; so practiced to kindle before havdalah — end; see below letter 4.
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: (ב) And further that blessing on Hanukkah light and its kindling contradicts the view of deferring the day's end, for it appears to reject and kindle Hanukkah light sanctifies Shabbat; he extended greatly; so Eliyah Rabbah in the name of Tosefet Yom Tov; Peri Chadash agreed with Taz — end; in synagogue do not change any custom; at home whoever follows his custom.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (ג) All the more in his house, etc., since he already made havdalah — meaning he already heard havdalah; his words are garbled — he did not intend to fulfill through the shaliach tzibbur's havdalah heard in synagogue. Know Taz and several Acharonim who uphold his method disagree on the Mechaber and Rama's essential law and hold havdalah mitzvah precedes Hanukkah light because it is frequent; see Biur Halacha we brought there is dispute among Rishonim; therefore in synagogue do not change custom practiced in Israel to kindle first then havdalah; at home whoever follows his custom.
peri-megadim/1:_: They kindle — ATZ in Terumat HaDeshen siman 60; so Beit Yosef in synagogue in the name of Maharil, Agur, Kol Bo like Terumat HaDeshen; as Mechaber ruled and Maharal of Prague holds like Radbaz Gor Aryeh z"l whom Tosefet Yom Tov brought (and responsum Maharil is Moharar Yaakov Levi z"l and Maharal of Prague is Moharar Yehuda Loew z"l); Eliyah Rabbah letter 1. What Taz wrote one may say frequent precedes — havdalah precedes Hanukkah light — as answer 1 Tosafot Bava Kamma 23b d.h. hadar; so siman 684 letter 3 and Magen Avraham there and two answers they wrote for the section; third answer: proof that losing also applies to publicizing miracle — we do not read haftarah for this; they wrote if so Hanukkah should precede and then Rosh Chodesh to read haftarah — Rosh Chodesh frequent precedes — all the more to defer Shabbos since haftarah has publicity; see Rosh z"l. What he wrote deferring day's end — one may reject frequent meaning superiority of frequent rejects deferring day's end and we make havdalah first; what he wrote Zevachim daf 90b and Rambam chapter 9 laws of additional offerings halacha 2 — whichever he wants he precedes as Kesef Mishnah there — the matter was not resolved; what he wrote in the name of Raavad z"l — Eliyah Rabbah explained on another matter — see there; siman 693 they read Megillah then make havdalah — also blessing me'orei esh arranged on cup except Taz z"l disagrees here to bless Hanukkah light then me'orei esh is not correct; likewise havdalah blessing — Taz brought at home he makes havdalah first then kindles; Levush says at home he makes havdalah then kindles — deferring day's end does not apply since he already made havdalah in synagogue — see there; impossible the Rav z"l practiced havdalah at home before Hanukkah light as Taz z"l ruled and as Levush; so I practice; do not rebuke anyone for he has whom to rely on. See Eliyah Rabbah explanation in Mordechai who holds also frequent precedes — nevertheless see there. Siman 688 seif 2 — per this Hanukkah light and one candle on the table suffice since we do not make havdalah on Hanukkah light — meaning borei me'orei ha'eish; see Levush.
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: Before. Avodat HaTodah; see in my responsa Beit Ephraim what he wrote on Terumat HaDeshen's words and explaining Taz's words and in responsum of Maharanch siman 79 regarding circumcision not in its time and pidyon haben — which precedes (see above siman 249 and siman 461 on Magen Avraham's words as Tosafot Moed Katan — circumcision every day is its time, forbidden to leave him uncircumcised) — in explanation of Rosh and Tur siman 286 — see there.
